I am 40, been farming since I was 15, finished middle school. I have 20 mu here in Quzhou, which is more land than most families around me, so I hire a tractor for rotary tilling and rent a combine for harvest. My wife helps on the farm, my parents look after the house, and my younger brother works in a factory in Handan and sends money home. That helps when I need to buy inputs, but I still count every yuan because a bad year hurts.

I always start from what I did last year. Last year my wheat made 530 kg per mu and my maize made 620 kg. This year I will push a little harder on fertilizer because prices for grain are steady.

For my 18 mu of wheat: I planted an improved variety, Jimai 22, last autumn. This spring I will topdress with 35 kg of urea per mu at green-up and another 15 kg per mu at jointing. Counting the basal compound fertilizer I put down at planting, the total for the season is about 18 kg of nitrogen, 7 kg of phosphorus, and 6 kg of potassium per mu. I will irrigate three times—green-up, jointing, and grain filling—using my well. I spray herbicide once and fungicide once. The land was rotary tilled before planting last fall. I expect 560 kg per mu if no late frost comes.

For the summer maize on the same 18 mu: After wheat harvest in June, I plant Zhengdan 958, a hybrid seed. I use no-till seeding now because it saves diesel and two days of labor, which matters when the weather window is tight. At planting I put 25 kg of compound fertilizer per mu, and at big trumpet stage I topdress with 30 kg of urea per mu. That comes to 20 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice, at jointing and filling. I spray pesticide three times total—once for weeds, twice for corn borer. I expect 650 kg per mu.

For stevia: I keep 2 mu by the well for this. I plant improved seedlings in mid-May. I apply 20 kg of compound fertilizer and 10 kg of potassium sulfate per mu, which is about 12 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium. Stevia drinks more water than grain, so I irrigate four times. I spray twice for insects. I rotary till before planting. Last year I got 280 kg of fresh leaves per mu; this year I want 300 kg. The buyer pays cash on delivery, which is good.

I thought about cutting back on fertilizer because urea went up 20 yuan per bag, but on 18 mu, losing even 30 kg of yield per mu would cost me more than the fertilizer. I would rather waste a little fertilizer than risk a bad harvest. That is how I manage.
